subject.title: [Bug]: Assistant text preceding a tool call in the same turn is silently dropped on Signal channel (Anthropic/Sonnet, non-streaming)

question: For source-channel `toolUse` turns that emit text before a tool call, should OpenClaw deliver that text, keep it private with an agent-visible undelivered marker, or require explicit message-tool delivery for user-visible confirmations?
rationale: The current source behavior is credible and harmful for confirmation workflows, but the opposite leak-prevention policy is also active; maintainers need to choose the durable delivery contract before an implementation can be safe.

options.title: Mark suppressed pre-tool text as undelivered
options.body: Keep commentary suppression for leak prevention, but record and inject delivery-state context so the model and transcript cannot treat unseen text as user-visible history.

options.title: Deliver classified user-visible pre-tool text
options.body: Flush only text that the runtime can classify as intentional user-facing output before tools, with tests proving commentary and internal narration remain suppressed.

options.title: Require explicit message tool delivery
options.body: Document pre-tool bare text as private and require `message(action=send)` or an equivalent explicit send path for channel-visible confirmations.

recommendation.title: Mark suppressed pre-tool text as undelivered
recommendation.body: Keep commentary suppression for leak prevention, but record and inject delivery-state context so the model and transcript cannot treat unseen text as user-visible history.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame spans the central suppression and payload paths, making this the strongest routing signal available from local history.
